narrative.overview:
Neutrino Rack Manager should feel like the quiet control layer of a semiconductor fabrication line: engineered, continuously observable, and deliberately uneventful until attention is required. Deep graphite and blue-black planes keep long sessions comfortable, while cool dividers and tabular facts turn a dense rack into an orderly instrument rather than a collection of dashboard cards.

The system is state-first and safety-first. Names, addresses, connectivity, and explicit text status remain visible before any control is considered; routine controls are restrained, and consequential actions only gain semantic warning color when revealed or confirmed. Light and dark themes share the same hierarchy and interaction logic rather than becoming separate visual identities.

Motion is brief and functional: it acknowledges state changes, loading, or transient notification entry. Surfaces remain grounded at rest, without decorative glow, gradients, or hover lift. The design rejects bright status mosaics, simultaneous rainbow actions, and ambiguous icon-only state.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite and blue-black tonal layering with a cool, low-saturation teal interaction accent.
Calm operational density: compact controls, legible full addresses, and stable rack geometry.
Explicit status text supported by semantic color, never replaced by it.
Flat, hairline-separated surfaces with depth reserved for overlays and transient layers.
Progressive disclosure for power actions, followed by scope-and-consequence confirmation.
Tabular numerals and monospace facts where operators compare addresses, counts, commands, or versions.

rules.name: The One Instrument Voice Rule
rules.body: Teal is the only non-semantic interaction accent; do not add another brand or navigation hue.

rules.name: The Text Before Hue Rule
rules.body: Every operational state is named in text first. Color may reinforce `Online`, `Offline`, `Partial`, `On`, `Off`, `Unknown`, `WARN`, or `ERR`, but may never carry that meaning alone.

rules.name: The Earned Alarm Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, and red appear only when live state, feedback, or action risk earns them; they are never used to decorate navigation, charts, or generic hierarchy.

rules.name: The Readout Integrity Rule
rules.body: Never truncate operational addresses, node names, versions, or confirmation scope merely to preserve a decorative composition; wrap safely or widen the fact column.

rules.name: The Quiet Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Build hierarchy through compact steps in weight, spacing, and tone. Avoid oversized headings that displace rack state from the first viewport.

rules.name: The Stable Rack Rule
rules.body: Responsive behavior may reflow node columns, but it must not reorder scope, hide operational identity, or collapse distinct OS, BMC, and Power state into one ambiguous summary.

rules.name: The Grounded Equipment Rule
rules.body: Persistent operational surfaces stay flat at rest. Do not add card lift, glow, glass blur, or decorative shadow to trays and nodes.

rules.name: The Overlay Earns Depth Rule
rules.body: Strong shadow is reserved for content that temporarily interrupts or floats above the operating plane.

rules.name: The Square Shoulder Rule
rules.body: Reuse the observed 4–14px corner ladder. Do not turn trays, node cells, workflow cards, or ordinary buttons into capsules.

dos: **Do** keep names, complete addresses, OS/BMC connectivity, and Power state ahead of controls in the reading order.
**Do** use nested neutral tones and 1px dividers to organize dense rack information before reaching for shadow.
**Do** preserve explicit `Healthy`, `Partial`, `Offline`, `Online`, `Off`, and `Unknown` language beside any semantic color.
**Do** reveal the seven power actions progressively and repeat scope plus consequence at confirmation.
**Do** preserve keyboard focus, reduced-motion behavior, tabular numerals, and the dark/light theme role mapping.
**Do** reserve monospace typography for facts operators compare exactly: IPs, commands, versions, and raw results.
donts: **Don't** decorate navigation, generic cards, or page chrome with green, amber, or red.
**Don't** present all power operations as a simultaneous rainbow button row.
**Don't** add hover lift, neon glow, glass blur, or ornamental gradients to persistent equipment surfaces.
**Don't** encode state with dots or color alone, and don't style normal Power Off as an error.
**Don't** use oversized marketing typography, pill-shaped cards, or airy spacing that pushes a complete tray out of the operating viewport.
**Don't** hide destructive scope, transport, confirmation requirements, or follow-up steps behind icon-only controls.
